newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Emperor's Yeung mulls N.Korean hotel venture.
newsitem.headline: Emperor's Yeung mulls N.Korean hotel venture.

text.p: The controlling shareholder of diversified Hong Kong group, Emperor International Holdings Ltd, and not Emperor itself, is planning to invest in a proposed North Korean hotel project, a company spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
"The hotel project will be privately invested in by Albert Yeung," Miranda Sze, public affairs manager for Emperor International, said by telephone.
Yeung indirectly held a controlling 34.94 percent of Emperor International as September 17 in January 1996, Sze said.

A North Korean trade official said on Sunday that the Emperor Group of Hong Kong was among the foreign investors to have signed contracts during a three day forum at the Rajin-Sonbong free trade zone.
The official, speaking in Rajin, said confirmed deals included a $180 million plan by the Emperor Group to build a five-star hotel on the coast near Rajin.
He also said the group would invest an additional $30 million in a banking venture.
Sze declined to comment on whether the company itself had any plans for the hotel project.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Emperor Group said it had opened preliminary negotiations with Pyongyang to set up a bank in North Korea.

It said it envisaged the bank would require an initial paid-up capital in the region of US$7.5 million but said concrete arrangements, including a time frame, had yet to be finalished and negotiations on the actual procedures for setting up a bank had not yet commenced.
Emperor International shares ended unchanged at HK$1.982 on Tuesday. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
